SECTION: unify_bullets

RUBRIC_REF: apps_rg/runtime/judges/employment_bullet_judge_rubric.py#unify_bullets

You are evaluating exactly 6 employment bullets (bul_unify_001..006).
This is a BULLET-LINE lane — not an executive summary paragraph.
Return JSON only with: score_scale, score, threshold, pass, decisive_failure, findings, cited_sentence_indexes, remediation_suggestions.

Score contract:
- score_scale must be "0_to_1" or "0_to_5" only.
- Keep score and threshold within the declared scale.
- Employment pool lanes: min_selection_score is the pass floor for Claude pool selection.

Rubric dimensions (employment bullets — not executive summary):
1. claim_ledger_grounding: each bullet maps to bul_* source_fact_ids in the claim ledger; metrics match allowed facts verbatim.
2. bullet_line_discipline: one high-impact resume bullet per slot — concise line, no narrative paragraph or multi-sentence block.
3. jd_briefing_targeting_discipline: JD and briefing shape emphasis only — never JD-as-proof, briefing-as-proof, or target company as experience.
4. keyword_discipline_without_stuffing: role-relevant phrasing without ATS keyword bags or copied JD phrases as proof.
5. cross_bullet_outcome_diversity: each bullet answers a distinct outcome spine — not six restatements of the same mechanism stack.
6. employer_scope_purity: no cross-employer fact leakage, wrong-company names, or facts from other employment slices.
7. current_role_unify_platform_signal: Unify reads as the candidate's current-role platform proof (governance, commercialization, scale) where evidenced.
8. protected_metric_anchor: bul_unify_006 preserves locked commercial metrics ($22M / margin / team scale) and approved metric_outcome_id anchors without splitting or diluting.
9. mechanism_inventory_cap: at most one mechanism-dense bullet; others stay outcome-led, not comma-stacked architecture inventories.

Decisive failure triggers:
- unsupported metric or cross-employer fact leakage (IBM/InsurTech/EY)
- first-person language
- wrong bullet count (expected 6)
- protected bul_unify_006 metrics missing or split incorrectly
- JD phrase copied as proof (>4 consecutive words)
- generic filler that loses Unify-specific mechanisms or protected metrics

Return ONLY one compact JSON object:
{"score_scale":"0_to_5","score":0.0,"threshold":4.0,"pass":true,"decisive_failure":false,
 "findings":["short strings"],"cited_sentence_indexes":[1],
 "remediation_suggestions":[],"rationale":"one short paragraph",
 "fail_reasons":[],"unsupported_claims":[],"quality_flags":[]}
score_scale must be 0_to_5 or 0_to_1 with in-range score/threshold.

  "briefing": "# Anthropic - Manager, Applied AI Architecture Partnerships briefing packet\n| Manager, Applied AI Architecture Partnerships | Compensation not disclosed | Reports to function not disclosed |\n\n## JD Complement\nAnthropic’s public position combines enterprise use of Claude with a stated focus on reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI. Customers and delivery partners need practical patterns for high-value workflows, while Anthropic benefits from keeping implementations product-centered, governable, and\nrepeatable rather than allowing every engagement to become a custom services project.\n\n## Company DNA & Operating Model\nAnthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation focused on AI safety and research. Its commercial model pairs a widely accessible AI product with an enterprise motion that depends on successful organizational adoption.\n\nClaude serves both business users and technical builders. That creates an operating environment where product capability, administrative controls, developer workflows, customer enablement, and partner delivery all affect realized value.\n\nThe company’s stated emphasis on safety, accuracy, security, reliability, interpretability, and steerability makes implementation quality commercially important. Architecture decisions must help customers achieve useful outcomes while\nmaintaining clear controls and appropriate use of the platform.\n\n## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure\nAnthropic’s enterprise materials present deployment as more than account access or a one-time technical event. Successful customer outcomes involve setup, organizational rollout, sustained usage, and refinement over time.\n\nThis creates pressure to translate frontier-model interest into durable, governed workflows. Customers need confidence that use cases can move beyond experimentation while remaining manageable for technology, security, procurement,\nbusiness, and administrative stakeholders.\n\nThe strategic challenge is to create clear interfaces among product teams, customer-facing technical teams, cloud providers, technology companies, services firms, and enterprise operators. Ambiguous ownership can lead to inconsistent\ndesigns, weak feedback loops, or delivery models that do not scale.\n\n## Leadership & Stakeholder Map\nThe relevant stakeholder map is cross-functional and ecosystem-oriented:\n\n- Product and engineering teams shape platform capabilities, technical constraints, and reusable solution boundaries.\n- Enterprise administrators influence identity, access, configuration, governance, and internal rollout.\n- Security, compliance, legal, and procurement groups affect customer readiness and buying confidence.\n- Cloud, technology, and services partners extend distribution, implementation capacity, and workflow expertise.\n- Customer sponsors, business teams, and developers determine whether early usage becomes durable operational adoption.\n\nThe role is likely valuable where these groups could otherwise optimize locally. Partners may prioritize delivery speed or client-specific requests, while product and enterprise teams need implementation standards that preserve\nquality and enable learning across deployments.\n\n## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals\nAnthropic’s narrative around reliable, interpretable, and steerable systems raises the standard for enterprise architecture. Conversations should center on controlled, useful production outcomes rather than generic AI enthusiasm or\nisolated demonstrations.\n\nClaude’s relevance to both business teams and developers creates a dual audience. Effective deployment patterns need to support technical integration and builder productivity while also addressing administration, governance, change\nmanagement, and broad employee use.\n\nEnterprise deployment guidance indicates that launch is an operating journey.
